facts.value: Consumes the bytecode stream through a monotonically advanced cursor, except when branch opcodes add encoded skip distances. Immediate operands are assembled from one, two, or four bytes; argument loads and literal loads prepend 32-bit values to an HSD_SList stack. Unary operations replace the top value, binary operations remove one node and combine it with the next, stack-control instructions discard or duplicate entries, and the return opcode reads the top as f32, removes every remaining node, and returns the value. A null bytecode pointer returns 0.0 immediately.

facts.value: Signature float HSD_ByteCodeEval(u8* bytecode, const f32* args, s32 nb_args). Instructions use one-, two- or four-byte big-endian immediates; stack nodes carry untagged 32-bit words reinterpreted as int, float or pointer in the target ABI. Argument loads assert operand < nb_args, but operand is u32 so negative nb_args converts to unsigned. There is no stream length parameter or general pointer/operand validation.

facts.value: Alternates opcode fetch and immediate collection. Opcode 3 consumes a raw nonzero word as a condition and pops it after an optional unsigned forward skip; opcode 4 always skips; opcode 1 reads top bits as f32 and frees all nodes. Most operand accesses assert stack depth, but opcode 5 repeatedly removes nodes and HSD_SListRemove(NULL) returns NULL, so over-discard does not assert. Missing duplicate depth, opcode 0xFF after one immediate byte, and unknown opcodes panic. Argument comparison is unsigned; byte-stream bounds, integer arithmetic and math-domain errors are not generally validated. Random opcodes advance the shared RNG.

facts.value: The local stack starts empty and decoding alternates between opcode fetch and one-, two- or four-byte immediate collection. Normal return frees the entire stack. Many invalid accesses assert or panic, but discard past an empty stack is tolerated by HSD_SListRemove. There is no input-length bound, opcode budget, signed argument-count validation, arithmetic overflow/divisor validation or recovery cleanup path for panics. Random operations mutate the shared generator.
